description: Document Filters is a toolkit that allows application developers to identify and extract metadata, as well as convert and render almost any file type. It is a core component of many products, but can also be leveraged as a stand-alone service for organizations or application developers.
releaseNotes:
# Enhancements

- Introduced support for extracting Microsoft Purview sensitivity label metadata from the modern LabelInfo stream format (SensitivityLabel_ prefix) in Office documents, in addition to existing extraction from legacy custom document properties (MSIP_Label_ prefix). This ensures consistent metadata extraction as Microsoft transitions to the new format. The new `SENSITIVITY_LABEL_MODE` option controls extraction behavior: `ALL` (default) extracts labels from both storage locations including removed labels for forensics and eDiscovery use cases, while `STRICT` skips removed labels and applies per-tenant filtering where any label from a tenant in the LabelInfo stream blocks all legacy custom properties from that same tenant, following the Microsoft specification for policy-unknown scenarios to extract the document's current labeling state. (DF-2896)

# Updates

- HD Mode: Resolved a condition for Apple Keynote files where large paragraphs could be cut off due to the absence of a ‘keepOnPage’ style option. This ensures that long paragraphs are preserved in the output, improving document fidelity and usability. (DF-2863)
- HD Mode: Resolved a condition for Apple Keynote files where list content could be shifted or missing in the output. This correction improves the accuracy and completeness of extracted data from Keynote presentations. (DF-2825)
- HD Mode: Resolved a condition for Apple Keynote files where the "Shrink Text to Fit" feature did not properly reduce the size of textboxes and paragraphs to fit within available space. This correction improves the fidelity of rendered presentations and ensures content is displayed as intended. (DF-2531)
- HD Mode: Resolved a condition for DOCX files where page numbering in document sections displayed the section number instead of the correct page number. (DF-2821)
- HD Mode: Resolved a condition for JPEG files where Document Filters could render oversized images when the source file stored resolution only in EXIF (no JFIF APP0 marker) and the `GRAPHIC_PNG_JPEG_DPI` option was enabled. The decoder now correctly reads DPI from EXIF resolution tags as a fallback, ensuring consistent page sizing for both JFIF and EXIF-only JPEGs. This improves accuracy and fidelity when rendering images from professional cameras and RAW processing software. (DF-2766)
- HD Mode: Resolved a condition for full-page image OCR where text was incorrectly scaled and misaligned in the rendered output when the `GRAPHIC_DPI` option was set and DPI scaling was performed. This ensures OCR text overlays accurately on background images, improving usability and fidelity for documents processed with custom DPI settings. (DF-2782)
- HD Mode: Resolved a condition where floating images or text boxes anchored inside a table that was split across multiple pages could cause "Error in IGR_Render_Page: Table children must be table rows" when converting to Markdown. (DF-2790)
- HD Mode: Resolved a condition where lines could be incorrectly split during paragraph layout. This correction ensures accurate line placement and improves document layout fidelity. (DF-2926)
- HD Mode: Resolved a condition where spacing after long words was rendered incorrectly and sometimes caused text overlap. (DF-2030)
- HD Mode: Resolved a condition where tab leaders in table of contents could extend too far and overlap with page numbers. (DF-2897)
- Resolved a condition for EML files where attachments with filenames containing emojis or 4-byte Unicode characters could not be extracted, resulting in an error or missing files. Attachments with emoji filenames are now correctly recognized and extracted, improving compatibility with modern email clients and internationalized content. (DF-2824)
- Resolved a condition for EML files where messages beginning with a header containing an underscore (such as msip_labels: ) were misidentified as Text/ASCII, resulting in excessively large PDF output. EML files with vendor-specific headers are now correctly identified, ensuring accurate rendering and extraction of email content. (DF-2834)
- Resolved a condition for OpenDocument Text (.odt) files where headers and footers were not extracted from documents generated by Microsoft Word or OpenOffice due to overly strict filtering on master page names. This ensures consistent extraction of header and footer content regardless of the application used to create the ODT file, improving accuracy for text extraction workflows. (DF-2809)
- Resolved a condition for PDF files where annotation text was incorrectly treated as document text, causing OCR to be suppressed on image-only PDFs with annotations. The OCR decision logic now distinguishes between annotation text and actual document text, ensuring OCR runs when the underlying page content is image-based. This restores expected text extraction for scanned PDFs and improves downstream search and AI workflows. (DF-2769)
- Resolved a condition for PNG files where they were incorrectly identified as Windows Metafile (WMF) format. This occurred when the WMF signature appeared within the first 2048 bytes of a PNG file, and the fix ensures accurate file type detection for improved processing reliability. (DF-2817)
- Resolved a condition for PST files where MSG subfiles with attachments larger than approximately 8 MB were truncated or corrupted during extraction, resulting in unreadable attachments. This restores full extraction of large email attachments, ensuring complete data import and downstream processing for legal discovery and similar workflows. (DF-2835)
- Resolved a condition for RTF and DOC files where converting to HD formats could cause a crash or segmentation fault if a header or footer contained an empty or missing paragraph. Files with these structures now process reliably, improving stability and preventing unexpected failures during conversion. (DF-2906)
- Resolved a condition for document processing where concurrent viewer requests could cause a crash in `DocumentFilters.GetAvailableOptions` due to a race condition in native code. The update adds proper locking to prevent simultaneous cache population, improving stability and reliability for environments with high concurrency. (DF-2929)
- Resolved a condition where enabling the `MARKDOWN_INCLUDE_LOCATIONS` option caused bounding boxes for text in textboxes to be reported relative to the textbox instead of the page. Bounding boxes are now correctly calculated relative to the page, improving location accuracy for downstream processing and analysis. (DF-2792)
- Security: freetype: CVE-2026-23865: patched: Applied security patch to address this issue. (DF-2830)
- Security: giflib: CVE-2026-23868: not-affected: The vulnerable function GifMakeSavedImage is not called by Document Filters. (DF-2845)
- Security: giflib: CVE-2026-26740: not-affected: The vulnerable function EGifGCBToExtension is not called by Document Filters. (DF-2872)
- Security: libpng: CVE-2026-33416: patched: Applied security patch to address this issue. (DF-2903)
- Security: libpng: CVE-2026-33636: patched: Applied security patch to address this issue. (DF-2904)
- Security: libpng: CVE-2026-34757: patched: Applied security patch to resolve this issue. (DF-2911)
- Security: libpng: CVE-2026-3713: not-affected: The pnm2png CLI tool is not built or included in Document Filters. (DF-2844)
- Security: libtiff: CVE-2025-61143: not-affected: The vulnerability is in the tiffcrop CLI tool. Document Filters does not compile or ship the tiffcrop CLI utility. (DF-2788)
- Security: libtiff: CVE-2025-61144: not-affected: The vulnerability is in the tiffcrop CLI tool. Document Filters does not compile or ship the tiffcrop CLI utility. (DF-2786)
- Security: libtiff: CVE-2025-61145: not-affected: The vulnerability is in the tiffcrop CLI tool. Document Filters does not compile or ship the tiffcrop CLI utility. (DF-2785)
- Security: libtiff: CVE-2026-4775: patched: Applied security patch to address this issue. (DF-2887)
- Security: openjpeg: CVE-2026-6192: patched: Applied security patch to address this issue. (DF-2916)
- Security: pdfium: CVE-2026-2648: patched: Applied security patch to address this issue. (DF-2778)
- Security: pdfium: CVE-2026-5889: not-affected: Vulnerable encryption creation path (FX_Random_GenerateMT) is never called — DF never creates or re-encrypts PDFs via pdfium. (DF-2907)
- Security: pdfium: CVE-2026-6305: patched: Applied security patch to resolve this issue. (DF-2920)
- Security: pdfium: CVE-2026-6306: patched: Applied security patch to resolve this issue. (DF-2919)
- Security: pdfium: CVE-2026-6361: patched: Applied security patch to resolve this issue. (DF-2917)
- Security: protobuf: CVE-2026-40027: false-positive: CVE-2026-40027 (path traversal in ALEAPP) was determined to be a false positive; ALEAPP is not present in Document Filters, and the vulnerability does not affect any included components. No action required. (DF-2908)
- Security: protobuf: CVE-2026-6409: not-affected: CVE-2026-6409 affects the Protobuf PHP PECL extension (versions < 4.33.6 and < 5.34.0-RC1), specifically php/src/Google/Protobuf/Internal/CodedInputStream.php. Document Filters uses the C++ protobuf library v3.0.0 compiled from source. (DF-2921)
- Security: skia: CVE-2026-3931: not-affected: The vulnerable code path does not exist in Document Filters. (DF-2843)
- Security: skia: CVE-2026-5870: not-affected: the vulnerable code path is not reachable; Skia is used only for 2D rasterization of document pages, not for HTML rendering. (DF-2909)
- Security: skia: CVE-2026-6298: patched: Applied security patch to resolve this issue. (DF-2923)
- Security: skia: CVE-2026-6364: not-affected: The vulnerability is in SkJpegMultiPicture.cpp (JPEG Multi-Picture Format parser), which is part of the modern SkCodec framework introduced after our Skia version. Document Filters uses a legacy version of Skia that predates the SkCodec API and does not contain the SkJpegMultiPicture module. (DF-2922)
- Security: skia: CVE-2026-7353: patched: Applied security patch to resolve this issue. (DF-2944)
- Security: skia: CVE-2026-7949: false-positive: CVE-2026-7949 requires a compromised Chrome renderer process and a crafted Chrome Extension to exploit, leaking cross-origin data between security contexts. Document Filters uses Skia exclusively as a 2D graphics rasterization backend for rendering document pages to bitmaps. (DF-2965)
- Security: snappy: CVE-2026-42154: not-affected: CVE-2026-42154 affects Prometheus, a monitoring system that uses snappy for request compression. The vulnerability is in Prometheus's remote read endpoint, not in the Google Snappy library itself. Prometheus is not present in Document Filters. (DF-2964)
- Security: tesseract: CVE-2026-26832: not-affected: CVE-2026-26832, a critical OS Command Injection vulnerability in the `node-tesseract-ocr` npm package, was reviewed and determined not to affect Document Filters. Document Filters uses the native Tesseract C++ library (version 3.02.02) and does not include or depend on the vulnerable JavaScript package, ensuring no exposure to this issue. No action is required for customers. (DF-2886)
- Security: xpdf: CVE-2026-4407: patched: Applied security patch to address this issue. (DF-2871)
- Security: zlib: CVE-2026-2229: not-affected: Document Filters does not use undici or Node.js. (DF-2861)
- Security: zlib: CVE-2026-23147: not-affected: This is a Linux kernel btrfs filesystem vulnerability, not a zlib library issue. (DF-2776)
- Security: zlib: CVE-2026-23943: not-affected: Document Filters does not use Erlang OTP or its SSH modules. This compression bomb vulnerability affects Erlang's SSH implementation, not zlib itself. (DF-2865)
- Security: zlib: CVE-2026-27171: not-affected: Document Filters never calls affected code. (DF-2779)
- Security: zlib: CVE-2026-27820: not-affected: CVE-2026-27820 affects the Ruby zlib gem (ruby/zlib), a Ruby-language binding for zlib, not the upstream C zlib library (madler/zlib). (DF-2925)
- Security: zlib: CVE-2026-3381: not-affected: The vulnerability is specific to a particular version of zlib which is not used by Document Filters. (DF-2833)
- Security: zlib: CVE-2026-35469: false-positive: CVE-2026-35469 is a vulnerability in moby/spdystream (a Go library for SPDY protocol multiplexing), not in the zlib C library. (DF-2924)
- Security: zlib: CVE-2026-39804: false-positive: CVE-2026-39804 is a vulnerability in Bandit (mtrudel/bandit), an Elixir HTTP server, not in the zlib C library. The 'zlib' association exists only because Bandit uses Erlang's zlib NIF internally, but the vulnerability is entirely in Bandit's application-level code. Document Filters does not use Elixir, Erlang/OTP, Bandit, or any WebSocket server. Document Filters uses the C zlib library version 1.3 directly from madler/zlib for compression/decompression with proper bounded buffers. (DF-2962)
- Security: zlib: CVE-2026-40036: false-positive: CVE-2026-40036 is a vulnerability in Unfurl (Python DFIR tool), not the zlib library. (DF-2910)
- Security: zlib: CVE-2026-4176: not-affected: CVE-2026-4176 is specific to Perl's bundled Compress::Raw::Zlib module, which vendors its own copy of zlib. Document Filters does not use Perl. (DF-2901)
- Security: zlib: CVE-2026-4738: not-affected: No code changes were required for CVE-2026-4738 (zlib-1.3: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer), as the vulnerability was already patched in a prior update. This ensures continued protection against out-of-bounds memory access when processing deflate64-compressed ZIP files, maintaining security for all users. (DF-2885)
summary: An SDK to identify, extract and view hundreds of file formats. Contains the Linux native binaries required to deploy with .NET core on Linux
